papers.title: WIMPs as FIMPs: the Inert Doublet Model and low-temperature reheating
papers.abstract: Weakly Interacting Massive Particles (WIMPs) are conventionally assumed to acquire their dark matter relic abundance through thermal freeze-out. However, this association relies on assumptions concerning the thermal history of the early Universe. We revisit the Inert Doublet Model (IDM), a representative WIMP framework in which dark matter interacts with the Standard Model through electroweak gauge interactions, even when its Higgs-portal coupling vanishes. We demonstrate that sufficiently low reheating temperatures can prevent chemical equilibrium, allowing a genuine WIMP to acquire its relic abundance through freeze-in rather than freeze-out. Considering both instantaneous and finite-duration reheating, we identify different production histories, including freeze-out during radiation domination, freeze-out during reheating, and freeze-in with potentially significant annihilation backreactions. These scenarios open regions of the IDM parameter space that would otherwise be excluded by dark matter overabundance. Our results demonstrate that WIMPs can behave as FIMPs, depending on the thermal history of the Universe.

papers.title: Weak magnetism effects on neutrino-nucleon interactions in hot nuclear matter within nonrelativistic Skyrme RPA
papers.abstract: Neutrino production, absorption, and scattering are important in explaining neutrino-driven core-collapse supernovae. At high densities or temperatures, relativistic effects, in particular weak magnetism (WM), may become increasingly important. Therefore, we extend the nonrelativistic random-phase approximation (RPA) framework for the study of neutrino-nucleon interactions in hot nuclear matter by incorporating the WM term into the nucleon weak current. In calculations with our recent Skyrme functional Sky3s, we confirm that WM increases interaction rates for the most important charged-current neutrino processes in supernovae and reduces those of antineutrinos. However, this is not the case for the antineutrino production via $\beta$ decay, which is also increased. In our calculations, WM can almost double the neutrino emissivities of neutron-star matter by direct Urca processes at high density. We also find that WM corrections to the scattering rates are increasingly important with increasing scattering angle and energy transfer, leading to a significant difference between double-differential neutrino and antineutrino scattering rates. Our formulas can help improve neutrino rates needed in supernova simulations.

papers.title: Early Evolution of Strange Quark Stars Admixed with Fermionic Dark Matter
papers.abstract: We study strange quark stars admixed with fermionic dark matter (DM) in three quasistatic stages of their early evolution: the neutrino-trapped stage, the heated stage after deleptonization, and the cold stage. Quark matter is described by the MIT bag model at finite temperature with thermal gluons, a repulsive vector interaction, and, in the first stage, trapped neutrinos. The DM is modeled as a cold, asymmetric gas of fermions with masses $m_\chi = 0.3$, $1$, and $3$ GeV, with and without a repulsive self-interaction, and interacts with the quark matter only through gravity. Using the two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff equations, we compute the structure, the maximum masses, and the tidal deformability of the stars in each stage for DM mass fractions $F_D$ up to $5\%$, and we follow individual stars at fixed numbers of baryons and DM particles. The effect of DM is nearly the same in the three stages: for $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the maximum mass by about $8\%$ and the tidal deformability of a $1.4\,M_\odot$ star by about $26\%$ in each stage, whereas the stage itself changes these quantities by only a few percent. Heavy DM forms a compact core; for $m_\chi = 3$ GeV without self-interaction, the mass limit of this core can set the maximum mass of the star. Light DM can form an extended halo, which does not increase the maximum mass for the fractions considered. For $m_\chi = 1$ GeV and $F_D = 5\%$, DM lowers the largest baryon mass of a newborn star by about $0.23\,M_\odot$, but this limit increases from the neutrino-trapped to the cold stage in all cases considered, so that DM does not cause a delayed collapse to a black hole. In our model, pulsars of about $2\,M_\odot$ require a stiff quark equation of state and restrict the DM fraction to a few percent unless the DM is light.

papers.title: Strong First-Order Phase Transition in a Pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone Boson Model
papers.abstract: We propose a novel, calculable model for realizing strong first-order phase transitions in the early Universe, in which the phase transition occurs along a pseudo-Nambu-Goldstone boson (pNGB) direction. The model involves two scalar fields whose interactions exhibit collective symmetry breaking, protecting the pNGB potential from quadratically divergent radiative corrections induced by these interactions. This structure allows strong first-order phase transitions to be realized without severe parameter tuning while maintaining perturbative control. We investigate the finite-temperature effective potential and bubble nucleation dynamics, identifying parameter regions where strong first-order phase transitions can successfully complete. The strength and characteristic time scale of the transitions are evaluated, and the resulting gravitational-wave (GW) spectra are computed. The predicted GW signals can fall within the sensitivity ranges of planned GW experiments.

papers.title: Dark matter mass fraction in axion stars
papers.abstract: QCD axion dark matter is fragmented into small mass miniclusters of high density. With the natural parameters of miniclusters, the time for Bose-Einstein condensation is less than the age of the Universe, which leads to the formation of Bose stars inside these structures. Recently, the problem of the subsequent growth of Bose stars was solved analytically (Dmitriev et al, Phys. Rev. Lett. 132, 091001 (2024)). We use this solution to determine present day mass fraction of dark matter in Bose stars and their mass function.

papers.title: The Sensitivity of Gamma-Ray Searches for Dark Matter Annihilation in Milky Way Dwarf Galaxies: the LSST Era and Beyond
papers.abstract: We forecast the sensitivity of gamma-ray searches to dark matter annihilation in Milky Way satellite dwarf galaxies using BabyBison, a Monte Carlo pipeline combining cosmological satellite simulations and observational selection functions with a joint likelihood analysis of gamma-ray data. Although LSST is expected to substantially expand the catalog of known satellite galaxies, we find that these discoveries are likely to produce only modest improvements in the resulting dark matter annihilation constraints, typically below 20\%. Much more substantial gains are possible, however, in relatively rare realizations that contain yet-to-be-discovered satellites with large $J$-factors. These results reinforce the fact that indirect detection analyses using the population of dwarf galaxies are typically driven in large part by a small number of high-$J$-factor systems rather than by the total satellite count. We present projections for the sensitivity of Fermi-LAT and the proposed Advanced Particle-astrophysics Telescope (APT) to dark matter annihilation, finding that a complete census of the Milky Way dwarf sample could enable such instruments to probe dark matter with masses up to the TeV scale. We also investigate the dark matter discovery potential of these instruments and project their ability to measure the properties of an annihilating dark matter particle.

papers.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
papers.abstract: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and E\"ot-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the E\"ot-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

papers.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
papers.abstract: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.

papers.title: Scotogenic dark matter from gauged $L_\mu+L_\tau$
papers.abstract: In this work, we introduce the first scotogenic model based on a gauged $L_{\mu} + L_{\tau}$ symmetry whose spontaneous breaking by two units leaves a remnant matter parity $M_P$. The resulting light active neutrinos are of Majorana nature and the lightest electrically neutral state mediating the scotogenic loop is stabilized by $M_P$ and can be identified as a weakly interacting massive particle dark matter candidate. We analyze the phenomenology of a predominantly singlet-like CP-even scalar dark matter candidate and the representative regions of parameter space compatible with the observed thermal relic abundance. The $Z'$ boson is compatible with a broad range of parameters relevant for dark matter. In particular, electroweak precision constraints do not lead to significant tensions for kinetic mixing values up to $\epsilon\sim 10^{-2}$. We discuss the implications of existing searches for leptophilic gauge bosons and the conditions under which visible and invisible collider signatures become relevant.

papers.title: Ionization of gravitational atoms by a companion-sourced Yukawa potential
papers.abstract: Superradiant instabilities around rotating black holes can produce clouds of ultralight bosons bound by the black hole's gravitational field. A binary companion can ionize these clouds by driving transitions into continuum states in the black hole's 1/r gravitational potential, extracting energy and angular momentum from the orbit. We investigate how a companion-sourced Yukawa interaction modifies this process. At weak coupling, the interference term between the gravitational and Yukawa transition amplitudes provides the leading correction to the ionization power. For the orbital frequencies here, an attractive interaction enhances continuum ionization and accelerates the inspiral, whereas a repulsive interaction has the opposite effect. At larger coupling, the pure Yukawa contribution to the ionization power becomes increasingly important and can compete with the gravitational contribution, particularly for lighter mediators. Comparing continuum ionization with off-resonant bound-state mixing, we find that continuum ionization can halt superradiant growth at a substantially smaller Yukawa coupling. At their respective critical couplings, the Yukawa interaction provides the dominant contribution to cloud depletion in both channels. Finally, we calculate the phase correction to gravitational waves due to continuum ionization and characterize how the chirp-rate response varies with frequency near the thresholds at which successive orbital harmonics open continuum-ionization channels.

papers.title: Higgs-portal dark matter beyond kinetic equilibrium
papers.abstract: We revisit the scalar, vector, and fermion Higgs-portal dark matter models in the resonant regime without assuming kinetic equilibrium during the freeze-out. We compute the relic abundance by solving the full momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation and compare the results with the standard momentum-averaged treatment. We find that the standard treatment significantly underestimates the relic abundance below the resonance, apart from the fermionic case with a purely scalar portal coupling where the difference is negligible. The deviation from the standard treatment is largest for fermionic models with pseudoscalar interactions, corresponding to factor of 10 in terms of the coupling that reproduces the correct relic abundance. For the scalar and vector cases the corresponding difference is up to a factor of 2. We confront the resulting parameter space with the latest constraints from direct and indirect detection, as well as collider experiments. We find the full momentum-dependent results systematically strengthen the direct detection constraints.

papers.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

papers.title: Long-Term Evolution of Hills-Captured Stars with TDE Disk Collisions: Links to Repeating Nuclear Transients
papers.abstract: Quasi-periodic eruptions (QPEs) and repeating partial tidal disruption event (rpTDE) candidates are widely interpreted as being powered by a star on an hours-to-years orbit around a massive black hole (MBH). Every such orbiter model presupposes a star delivered onto an extraordinarily compact orbit without being destroyed, but it is unclear whether this is achievable. We follow the coupled orbital and stellar evolution of stars captured by the Hills mechanism, combining gas drag and per-collision mass loss from recurrent TDE disks with gravitational-wave (GW) orbital decay and stochastic two-body relaxation in a Monte Carlo model. Conventionally, the EMRI-formation criterion is based on comparing the timescales of GW decay and orbital angular momentum relaxation. We find that this criterion severely overestimates the EMRI rate: for relaxation timescales shorter than a Hubble time, most Hills-captured stars are tidally disrupted before GW emission can circularize the stellar orbit. Instead, TDE-disk drag plays a crucial role in the orbital evolution and can boost the fraction of stars reaching QPE orbits by an order of magnitude or more, assuming that the disk aspect ratio is relatively large $H/r \sim 0.1$. We also find that collisional ablation imposes a minimum orbital period that rises with MBH mass and precludes sub-day orbits for $M_{\rm BH} \gtrsim 10^6\,M_\odot$, unless GWs alone can drive orbital decay faster than orbital relaxation. This can explain the observed preference of short-period QPEs for low-mass MBHs. Most known rpTDEs lie below the Hills-capture period minimum and thus require additional orbital decay, which TDE-disk drag can plausibly supply. These results support the viability of the orbiter model; our predictions of the MBH mass and orbital period distributions can be used to further test this model.

papers.title: Effect of dark matter and scalar-cut potential on the macroscopic properties of neutron stars: A chiral quark mean field approach
papers.abstract: We investigate the effects of fermionic dark matter (DM) and scalar-cut potential ($U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$) on the equation of state (EOS) and macroscopic properties of neutron stars. The baryonic matter consists of neutrons, protons, electrons, and muons under the $\beta$-equilibrium and is described within the chiral SU(3) quark mean-field (CQMF) model. In this framework, quarks are confined within baryons, whose properties are modified through the exchange of scalar fields $\sigma$, $\zeta$, and $\delta$, and vector fields $\omega$ and $\rho$. The DM is modelled as a self-interacting fermionic fluid with scalar $\varphi_D$ and vector $V_D^\mu$ mediators. The baryonic and DM fluids interact only through gravity and are treated within a two-fluid Tolman-Oppenheimer-Volkoff formalism. We examine the resulting mass-radius relation and tidal deformability, along with the gravitational redshift, to investigate the effects of DM on neutron star structure and observable properties. The inclusion of $U_{\text{cut}}(\phi)$ stiffens the EOS, whereas increasing the DM fraction generally softens the EOS and modifies the mass-radius relation, tidal deformability, and gravitational redshift. The magnitude and nature of these modifications depend on the DM particle mass and mediator interactions, which determine whether the resulting configurations exhibit compact DM cores or extended DM halos.

papers.title: Finite-temperature quark dynamics in proto-neutron stars: Maximum baryonic mass and radial oscillations
papers.abstract: Finite-temperature quark dynamics can significantly alter proto-neutron star evolution even when the cold equation of state remains unchanged. We quantify this sensitivity by comparing a purely hadronic baseline with two hybrid models incorporating quark matter via the Polyakov-Nambu-Jona-Lasinio (PNJL) framework and its entanglement extension (EPNJL), which isolates the role of finite-temperature chiral-deconfinement coupling. Employing bulk Gibbs constructions for both nuclear liquid-gas and hadron-quark phase coexistence, we compute equilibrium configurations across hot neutrino-trapped, hot neutrino-free, and cold stages, alongside linear radial oscillations of selected hot neutrino-free stars. Introducing quarks lowers the maximum baryonic mass at every stage and reverses its evolutionary ordering: whereas the maximum baryonic mass increases toward the cold limit in the purely hadronic model, it decreases progressively in both hybrid models, opening mass windows for delayed collapse. Crucially, despite sharing the same cold limit, PNJL and EPNJL yield distinct baryonic-mass intervals for mixed-core survival across stages: only EPNJL permits configurations that retain mixed cores across both hot stages, whereas only PNJL allows hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars to possess cold equilibrium counterparts. All tested hot neutrino-free mixed-core stars remain linearly stable, yet their fundamental radial frequencies differ substantially. These findings demonstrate that finite-temperature quark dynamics imprints distinct evolutionary constraints and pulsation signatures on proto-neutron stars beyond cold-matter descriptions.

papers.title: Evolution and Prospects of Higgs Boson Searches Beyond the Standard Model
papers.abstract: The search for Higgs bosons Beyond the Standard Model (BSM) began intensively at the Large Electron-Positron (LEP) collider (1989-2000), continued at the Tevatron (2001-2011), and entered a new era with the start of the Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in 2010. While the discovery of a Higgs boson in 2012 established the Standard Model mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking, it also opened a wide landscape of open questions that motivate ongoing BSM Higgs searches. This review traces the evolution of these searches across experiments, highlighting both experimental techniques and underlying theoretical ideas in an accessible manner. Emphasis is placed on how different collider environments shaped search strategies and how seemingly subtle experimental effects, such as small excesses, non-standard decay topologies, or suppressed couplings, can provide insight into the possible structure of extended Higgs sectors. By connecting historical developments with current analyses and future prospects, this article aims not only to summarise results but also to provide students and newcomers with intuitive insight into how Higgs searches are designed, interpreted, and continuously refined. It illustrates how experimental challenges translate into physics opportunities, thereby inviting the next generation of researchers to contribute to one of the central questions in particle physics: whether the Higgs sector is minimal or part of a more complex structure.

papers.title: Thermodynamics of QCD+QED from the lattice
papers.abstract: QED corrections to observables in QCD are by now well-understood at zero temperature, where QED effects are perturbative and required for precision physics observables, such as the neutron-proton mass difference or the muon anomalous magnetic moment, among many others. However, there are indications in the literature that at finite temperature the introduction of QED can lead to non-perturbative effects, affecting the structure of the phase diagram, since the combined theory is exactly center-symmetric. In this proceedings article, we analyze the structure of the combined theory and the different strategies to simulate it on the lattice, as well as presenting novel results of lattice QCD+QED simulations at finite temperature, focusing on understanding the role of the electromagnetic coupling in the thermodynamics of this system. We also discuss new features that arise in the combined theory and the challenges that these simulations entail, which require the development of new algorithms in order to understand the phase diagram of QCD+QED from first principles.

papers.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
papers.abstract: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

papers.title: Scale-dependent Dark Matter in a Multi-component Cosmological Framework: Distinct Components Governing Galactic and Cosmological Dynamics
papers.abstract: In this work we generalize the concept of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter from galactic to cosmological scales. At galactic scales, the scale-dependent equation of state which successfully describes dark matter dominated galaxies has a nearly isothermal equation of state of the form $P(r)=K(r)\rho(r)$, where the entropy function $K(r)$ is radius dependent and slowly varying with the galactic radius. Using appropriate theoretical arguments, the successful galactic scale dark matter model is generalized to have a universal equation of state of the form $\langle P(\chi)\rangle =\langle \rho(\chi)\rangle \langle \sigma_{DM}^2\rangle$, where $\chi$ is the scale of the system under study and it can describe cosmological or galactic scales and $\sigma_{DM}$ is the characteristic velocity dispersion of dark matter at the relevant scales. This results to the entropy function behaving universally as $K(\chi)=\langle \sigma_{DM}^2\rangle$. We investigate the cosmological implications of scale-dependent equation of state dark matter, and we conclude that this scale-dependent equation of state dark matter cannot be the sole component of dark matter in the Universe. Also the second aim of this work is to provide a sufficient explanation for the question why $K_0$ changes for each galaxy, where $K_0$ is the value of $K(r)$ at intermediate and large radii from the core of the galaxy. Furthermore, we introduce the concept of having distinct dark matter components which cluster differently, and thus controlling differently the dynamics of the Universe at various scales. Scale-dependent equation of state dark matter can control the galactic scales, while another component can dominate at cosmological scales and thus control the Universe at cosmological scales.

papers.title: Quantifying the Impact of Galactic Dark Matter Halo Models on LZ Results
papers.abstract: Most dark matter direct-detection limits are reported under the assumption of an isotropic, Maxwellian Standard Halo Model. However, the Milky Way's stellar halo exhibits substantial radial anisotropy, while cosmological simulations predict scale-dependent anisotropy in the dark matter velocity distribution. We investigate how departures from isotropy affect the interpretation of LZ results in two complementary regimes: background-dominated elastic-scattering searches and the recently reported 248 keV nuclear-recoil candidate, which we study using a background-free single-event approximation. For elastic scattering, we use the self-consistent isotropic, Osipkov-Merritt, axisymmetric, and triaxial halo models of Belli et al. and translate the published limits through the ratio of predicted event counts, applying a common escape-speed truncation in the Galactic frame. At WIMP masses above approximately 40 GeV, the resulting limits lie within about $\pm 30\%$ of the isotropic reference. Below approximately 15 GeV, the model envelope broadens to as much as an order of magnitude, reflecting sensitivity to the high-velocity tail. For the 248 keV event, the accessible inelastic mass splitting is likewise controlled by this tail. Some anisotropic models extend the allowed kinematic region towards splittings at which solar-neutrino constraints on a Higgsino interpretation become ineffective, although kinematic accessibility alone does not establish viability at the fixed Higgsino cross section. These results show that halo-model dependence is modest at high WIMP masses but becomes essential near kinematic thresholds.

papers.title: Constraining Gamma-Ray Emission Beyond the TOV Limit: A Targeted Fermi-GBM Search for Counterparts to 39 LVK Gravitational-Wave Candidates in GWTC-5.0
papers.abstract: We present a systematic search for sub-threshold gamma-ray counterparts within a one-day time window of 161 gravitational-wave (GW) events from the GWTC-5.0 catalog, whose inferred source masses exceed the adopted Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) limit, using the Gamma-ray Targeted Search (GTS) pipeline. The search identifies 39 candidate GW--gamma-ray pairs satisfying the adopted joint likelihood-ratio thresholds. None of these candidates exhibits a temporal offset compatible with the prompt-emission delay observed for GW170817 ($\sim 1.7$ s); the smallest temporal separation is 17 min 17.976 s, ruling out GW170817-like prompt temporal associations in our candidate sample. Several candidates nevertheless show substantial spatial consistency. In particular, the most spatially consistent pair has a joint localization overlap of 95.4%, despite a temporal separation of 13 h 19 min 8.85 s, illustrating that high spatial agreement can occur by chance in the absence of temporal consistency. Among the sub-threshold gamma-ray candidates, we further identify an anomalous event with an exceptionally large single-instrument significance of log LR = 5250.84. For comparison, the adopted $3\sigma$ threshold corresponds to log LR $\approx 9$. The extreme likelihood ratio of this candidate motivates further investigation of trigger sensitivity, onboard veto configurations, and the statistical interpretation of sub-threshold events. Overall, we find no physically viable multi-messenger associations between the GWTC-5.0 events and the searched gamma-ray candidates, and derive corresponding upper limits on prompt high-energy emission from GWTC-5.0 progenitors.

papers.title: Four consistent estimates of $H_0$ from a $\Lambda$CDM inference network given CMB data
papers.abstract: We organize inferences from cosmic microwave background (CMB) data, of the current rate of expansion, $H_0$, into a network whose structure is informed by a scaling symmetry of the Einstein-Boltzmann evolution equations. There are four distinct routes through this network from a calibrating anchor to $H_0$. Given key assumptions of the $\Lambda$CDM model, they are mutually consistent. This consistency is a significant feature of the $\Lambda$CDM model's compatibility with CMB data. The redundancy in $H_0$ determinations illuminates a hurdle to resolving the $H_0$ tension with alternative cosmological models.

papers.title: A Minimal Toy Model of Charged Superradiant Spin-Down in Extreme-Mass-Ratio Inspirals
papers.abstract: Long-lived extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) are sensitive to slow changes in the mass and spin of their central black holes. We construct a deliberately minimal toy model in which an effective hidden charge opens a charged-superradiance channel, a bosonic cloud grows from a seed, and energy and angular momentum are transferred from a rotating black hole to the cloud. The model is not a Kerr-Newman perturbation calculation. Instead, it consists of a threshold function, one phenomenological rate coefficient, and balance equations that conserve the combined black-hole-cloud energy. This reduction yields an analytic relation between mass loss and spin-down and makes the roles of the growth coefficient, seed energy, and superradiant margin transparent. For an illustrative system with initial mass $2\times10^6 M_\odot$, spin 0.90, effective charge-to-mass ratio 0.30, and a one-year evolution time, the chosen benchmark reaches $M/M_0=0.8933$ and $a_\star=0.7704$. These values are then passed to FastEMRIWaveforms as two stationary Kerr snapshots. The resulting figures show that the endpoint state has a shifted time-domain oscillation pattern and a lower-frequency harmonic structure relative to the initial state. Because the snapshots are regenerated independently, they do not constitute a phase-connected, time-dependent waveform and cannot by themselves support a detectability claim. The value of the construction is instead diagnostic: it isolates a compact set of assumptions, exposes parameter degeneracies, and identifies the minimum ingredients required for a future self-consistent calculation. In this sense, the model provides a reproducible bridge between charged-superradiance intuition and EMRI waveform studies without presenting its benchmark as an astrophysical forecast.

papers.title: Offsets in gravitational wave burst timing in eccentric black hole binaries with stellar-mass tertiaries
papers.abstract: At present, the formation scenarios producing observed compact binary coalescences (CBCs) are relatively unconstrained. Such mergers are thought to occur efficiently in hierarchical triple systems, with three-body dynamics and stellar interactions from the tertiary inducing mergers in the inner binary. Deducing the presence of a tertiary in an observed gravitational wave (GW) signal from a merging binary would be a smoking gun for this specific formation scenario, offering constraints on the evolution of CBC progenitors and multiple star systems. We present a fast model for the effect of tertiary perturbation on observed GW signals from generically-oriented eccentric inner binaries. We apply the model to two populations of triples with merging inner binaries: (1) a group of wide triples whose inner binary was driven to merger through excitations of the inner eccentricity due to three-body dynamics and von Zeipel-Lidov-Kozai (ZKL); and (2) compact triples with chemically homogenously evolving (CHE) inner binaries that merge after experiencing mass transfer from the tertiary companion. When viewed face-on, the expected offset in the burst arrival time for the compact (CHE) triples varies by orders of magnitude depending on the properties of the triple system, with the majority of systems having an offset between $10^{-2}$ to $10^2$ seconds. A smaller fraction of the population with the highest inner eccentricities show the largest offset at $10^3$ to $10^6$ seconds. For the wide (ZKL) systems, the vast majority experience negligible perturbation from the tertiary. With an inclination of $\pi/2$ with respect to the observer both the compact and wide triple populations are expected to have offsets on the order of $10^3$ to $10^4$ seconds.

papers.title: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals: accessing generic orbits
papers.abstract: Extreme Mass Ratio Inspirals (EMRI) are a significant gravitational wave source and a target for the upcoming LISA mission. Computations of the fluxes of conserved quantities, such as energy and angular momentum, are a critical part of modeling EMRI waveforms and can be performed using a frequency domain formalism to solve the Teukolsky equation. This requires computations of large numbers of mode amplitudes, many of which are negligible. However, it is unknown ex ante which can be safely skipped. We present a machine learning approach to estimate the dominant radial mode number as a function of the remaining mode numbers and apply it to reduce the number of unnecessary computations in EMRI flux calculation.

papers.title: Measuring the Neutrino Mass with $^{241}$Pu
papers.abstract: Tritium has long been the isotope of choice for measurements of the absolute neutrino mass. Its low nuclear mass leads to substantial recoil energy, limiting measurements with both molecular tritium ($T_2$) and atomic tritium bound to a substrate. With a beta-decay endpoint energy and half-life similar to those of tritium, but a much larger nuclear mass, $^{241}$Pu may offer an interesting alternative. Its principal challenge is background from the beta decay of $^{237}$U. We discuss strategies for suppressing this background and compare the projected neutrino-mass sensitivities of $^{241}$Pu and tritium as a function of the background suppression.

papers.title: Neutron lifetime puzzle and Dicke coherence in spontaneous decays
papers.abstract: The long-standing discrepancy between beam and bottle measurements of the free-neutron lifetime---known as the neutron lifetime puzzle---remains an open anomaly in nuclear and particle physics. Here, we investigate whether collective quantum synchronization via macroscopic Dicke superradiance can influence free-neutron decay or mediate the relaxation of hypothetical excited neutron states. We show that superradiance is fundamentally obstructed in standard three-body weak beta decay by continuous final-state phase space and fermionic antisymmetrization, and remains inactive in terrestrial ultracold neutron traps due to low particle densities, even within the Koch--Hummel excited-neutron model. Extending this analysis to the primordial plasma prior to Big Bang nucleosynthesis, we demonstrate that rapid $e^\pm$ collisional dephasing and intense thermal photon backgrounds prevent a superradiant purge and instead enforce thermal detailed balance. Consequently, across the entire parameter space unconstrained by terrestrial experiments, an excited neutron state inevitably thermalizes before weak freeze-out, increasing the effective neutron statistical weight and severely overproducing primordial $^4\text{He}$, thereby excluding the standard realization of the Koch--Hummel hypothesis.

papers.title: Dual Horizon-MAD: A New Mode of Binary Black Hole Magnetically Arrested Accretion with Saturated Horizon Magnetic Fluxes and Intermittent Minidisks
papers.abstract: Reliable first-principles predictions of multimessenger signals from inspiralling supermassive binary black holes (SMBBHs) require magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulations in full general relativity (GR) that resolve the accretion flow down to the black hole horizons. However, performing such simulations long enough to relax the magnetohydrodynamics near the BBHs is computationally challenging and a source of uncertainty in modeling efforts. In this work, we present the longest MHD simulation of circumbinary disk (CBD) accretion onto a SMBBH in full GR. The equal-mass, quasicircular, nonspining BBH starts at an initial separation of $d/M=30$ and evolves over $\sim56$ orbits ($t \simeq 52,000 \, GM/c^3$), relaxing the magnetic field dynamics within the CBD cavity. After $\sim 23$ orbits and persistent magnetically arrested minidisks, the accretion enters a new magnetically arrested mode which we call dual horizon-MAD (DH-MAD). In DH-MAD, the dimensionless horizon magnetic fluxes remain saturated at $\phi_{BH}\sim 20$ driving magnetic flux eruptions from the vicinity of the BH horizons, and the vertical magnetic flux in the cavity saturates, but no flux eruptions occur at the cavity-CBD boundary. During this DH-MAD phase, there is also a shift in the total mass accretion rate variability, which exhibits a periodicity of $f\sim 1.8 f_{\rm orb}$, while the accretion rate modulation on the individual black holes occurs almost at the orbital period, $f\sim 0.9 f_{\rm orb}$. $\phi_{BH}$ also exhibits a robust periodicity at $f\sim 0.4 f_{\rm orb}$, suggesting that quasiperiodic nonthermal emission from magnetic reconnection near the horizons could be a smoking gun electromagnetic counterpart to inspiraling SMBBHs. Finally, minidisks around the BHs become intermittent in the DH-MAD phase, even at a separation of $d/M = 24$, likely due to the large plasma magnetization in the optically thin cavity.

papers.title: A Cross-Domain Simulator and Benchmark for Uncertainty Quantification in Global 21-cm Inference
papers.abstract: End-to-end uncertainty propagation in scientific inference often requires repeated evaluation of coupled simulators spanning multiple physical domains, often at prohibitive computational cost. Global 21-cm cosmology is an extreme example: a millikelvin cosmological signal must be separated from radio foregrounds and instrumental effects four orders of magnitude larger, making inference acutely sensitive to model misspecification. Reliable recovery is therefore contingent on an exceptionally accurate model that jointly propagates uncertainty through the complete observational chain. We present a differentiable, GPU-accelerated hybrid forward model combining neural emulation of the cosmological signal, a physics-informed multi-resolution parameterisation of the galactic foregrounds, and a linear surrogate model of the antenna. This unifies simulators spanning astrophysics and computational electromagnetics while reducing evaluation time by a factor of $7.2\times10^{7}$. Using GPU-accelerated Nested Slice Sampling, we benchmark the framework across 100 unseen signal realisations and find that 94 injected profiles lie entirely within their corresponding 95% credible bands. Together, the simulator and reference Nested Slice Sampling results provide a demanding benchmark of posterior calibration, mode coverage, and evidence accuracy across next-generation stochastic samplers, simulation-based inference, and variational inference frameworks.

papers.title: Wavelet-CFM for the extragalactic millimeter-wave sky
papers.abstract: We develop a Wavelet-factorized Conditional Flow Matching (Wavelet-CFM) framework to generate fast, accurate simulations of correlated astrophysical fields including gravitational lensing convergence ($\kappa$), the kinetic and thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich (kSZ and tSZ) effects, and cosmic infrared background (CIB) emission. Together these make up every bright extragalactic component of the millimeter-wave (mm-wave) sky apart from radio sources. Our approach combines multi-scale wavelet decomposition with conditional flow matching models, trained on $\sim$9$\times$9 deg$^2$ patches at 1-arcminute resolution. The four fields are generated jointly, including their cross couplings, and the model has a tractable likelihood, which to our knowledge has not previously been achieved for this set of components. The power spectra, one-point distributions and Minkowski functionals of the generated maps match a validation set to a few percent. These results show promise for enabling field-level cosmological analyses of mm-wave data.

papers.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
papers.abstract: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

papers.title: Radiation-Hydrodynamical Modeling of Accretion Columns in Ultraluminous X-ray Pulsars
papers.abstract: Ultraluminous X-ray pulsars (ULXPs) provide a unique laboratory for studying accretion-column physics under strongly magnetized super-Eddington conditions. In this work, we employ a one-dimensional radiation-hydrodynamical model to investigate the vertical structure of ULXP accretion columns, applying it to NGC 300 ULX-1, Swift J0243.6$+$6124, and SMC X-3. We solve the coupled conservation equations for the inflowing gas and radiation field in a dipole-funnel geometry, allowing the velocity, density, gas pressure, radiation pressure, total energy transport rate, radiation sonic surface, and thermal mound location to be determined self-consistently. We find that radiation pressure naturally produces an extended sinking region above the stellar surface, where the inflowing gas is gradually decelerated and its kinetic energy is converted into radiation energy that partly escapes through the column walls. Despite their different luminosities, magnetic fields, and column geometries, the radiation sonic surfaces are tightly clustered near $15$ km, indicating a similar large-scale radiative deceleration structure. These results show that ULXP accretion columns develop extended radiation-dominated structures regulated by the mass accretion rate, magnetic scattering opacity, and column geometry. The dynamical profiles obtained here provide a physical basis for interpreting radiation-dominated accretion columns in ULXPs and for future physics-based spectral modeling.

papers.title: Extragalactic carbon-monoxide (CO) as a CMB foreground: an analytic halo model for the CO auto-spectrum and its correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background
papers.abstract: Context. Carbon Monoxide (CO) lines emitted by star-forming galaxies are redshifted into the frequency bands of the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) experiments. Their correlation with the Cosmic Infrared Background (CIB) may be a non-negligible small-scale foreground. Aims. We develop an analytic, full-shape halo model framework for the CO auto-spectrum and for the CO$\times$CIB cross-spectrum in CMB bands, and assess its impact on current and future high-resolution CMB experiments. Methods. We use a luminosity-weighted halo model with separate occupation distributions of central and satellite galaxies for CO and CIB emitters, CO transitions up to $J=13$, and all auto- and cross-frequency spectra. Line and infrared luminosities derive from the same star formation rate. We perform Fisher analysis for ACT-like and CMB-HD-like experiments. Results. At $\ell=3000$, the CO$\times$CIB contribution to the sky power is 0.4, 0.7, and 1.9 $\mu$K$^2$ at 90, 150, and 220 GHz, and the CO auto-spectrum is $\simeq0.02\,\mu$K$^2$. For an ACT-like experiment, the CO occupation parameters are essentially unconstrained, and neglecting CO leaves the cosmological parameters unbiased, but shifts the radio and SZ parameters by $\sim2\sigma$ and $\simeq1\sigma$, respectively. For a CMB-HD-like experiment, CO is detected with high significance and the minimum halo masses of CO and CIB emitters are constrained; neglecting CO biases the cosmological parameters up to $\sim2\sigma$ when all multipoles are used in the analysis. Conclusions. CO should be included in the foreground model of future high-resolution CMB analyses; our framework describes it analytically and consistently with the CIB, and the code implementing it is publicly available.

papers.title: Why High-Spin Prograde MAD States Are Not Realized for AGN in Nature: Consequences for AGN Phenomenology
papers.abstract: Quasar-like and other bright active galactic nuclei are typically radio quiet despite strong evidence that many host rapidly spinning black holes. In contrast, general relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations show that high-spin prograde black holes in magnetically arrested disk (MAD) states produce the most powerful relativistic jets. We show that these results are not in conflict but instead correspond to physically distinct and mutually limiting evolutionary pathways. If accretion proceeds through radiatively efficient thin disks, then as the innermost stable circular orbit decreases with increasing prograde spin, radiative output and radiation pressure rise sharply, driving strong disk winds that remove the conditions required for effective jet formation. In this branch, high-spin prograde systems are therefore expected to be jet-suppressed. Alternatively, if accretion transitions to radiatively inefficient flows capable of producing MAD states, then the spin-up to near-maximal prograde rotation proceeds on timescales that exceed the age of the universe for the relevant systems, preventing the realization of the extreme high-spin prograde MAD configurations explored in GRMHD simulations. Within this framework, powerful jets need only be produced efficiently in counterrotating systems, not maximized there, preserving the time-dependent spin evolution central to the counterrotation versus corotation paradigm of Garofalo et al. (2010). We thus reconcile GRMHD results with observations and provide a unified interpretation of the radio-loud/radio-quiet dichotomy and the cosmic evolution of powerful radio sources.

papers.title: Light on GeV-scale seesaw
papers.abstract: The next generation of beam-dump and accelerator-neutrino experiments will probe GeV-scale sterile neutrinos with unprecedented sensitivity. However, the tiny active-sterile mixing predicted by the minimal seesaw mechanism is expected to remain out of reach. Oscillation data require at least two sterile neutrinos, $N_1$ and $N_2$, which may couple to the photon through a transition dipole. Such a coupling can radically change the picture, both by strongly enhancing sterile-neutrino production and by opening new decay channels. We identify charged-lepton pairs produced by an off-shell photon as the most promising experimental signature. We show that the seesaw band can be probed by the T2K near detector for sterile-neutrino masses $m_N\lesssim 500$ MeV, and by SHiP for $m_N\lesssim 5$ GeV. For a sufficiently large dipole, $d\gtrsim (10~\mathrm{TeV})^{-1}$, SHiP can selectively measure decay channels that require nonzero active-sterile mixing. This would give rise to a distinctive hierarchy of signatures, providing a direct test of the seesaw mechanism.

papers.title: Design of a Resonator Array Axion Haloscope and its Projected Sensitivity from 2 to 4 GHz
papers.abstract: The QCD axion is a dark matter (DM) candidate particle which can also solve the long-standing strong charge-parity problem. The Axion Dark Matter eXperiment (ADMX) searches for resonantly-enhanced conversion of axion DM into photons in a strong magnetic field. Previous versions of the experiment probed most QCD axion DM from 2.7 $\mu$eV to 4.2 $\mu$eV, with ongoing and planned runs poised to cover up to 8 $\mu$eV (2 GHz). We present the design of a haloscope with 18 cavities 1 m in length read out using individual low-noise amplifier chains and digital coherent signal combination called ADMX extended frequency range (EFR). We discuss details on magnet and cryogenic infrastructure, cavity design, cold electronics and efficiency of coherent signal combination. We use detailed cavity and electronics simulations, as well as diagnostic data from previous ADMX runs, to estimate frequency-dependent instantaneous scan rate. When paired with a comprehensive study of experiment downtime, a projection of final axion coupling sensitivity is produced. Under the stated assumptions, the projected sensitivity is projected to reach below the DFSZ axion benchmark model from 8 $\mu$eV to 16 $\mu$eV (2 GHz to 4 GHz) in 36 months.

papers.title: Using fixed $w$ to reproduce evolving $w_0$-$w_a$ dark energy at the field level
papers.abstract: Recent results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) hint at dynamical dark energy, making the accurate modelling of such cosmologies increasingly important for future analyses. In this work, we show that because, when written in superconformal time $\tau$, the $N$-body equations of motion depend on the background cosmology only through the expansion history $a(\tau)$, matching $a(\tau)$ allows us to map one cosmology onto another. As a first, observationally relevant, application of this new method, we match a Chevallier--Polarski--Linder (CPL) cosmology to a constant-$w$ cosmology with the closest $a(\tau)$. This allows us to use a single fixed-$w$ simulation to reproduce the simulation predictions of the target CPL cosmology at the field level at redshifts $0\le z\le3$. We validate this matching with 100 pairs of CPL and fixed-$w$ \textsc{mg-glam} simulations, spanning $0.1\le\Omega_{\rm m}\le0.5$, $-1.4\le w_0\le-0.5$ and $-1.8\le w_a\le-0.15$. For a DESI-like cosmology, the matter power spectra of the matched and target simulations agree to 0.24\% for $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ and 0.8\% up to $k\lesssim3\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at $0\le z\le3$, and the density phases are reproduced with a stochasticity below 0.02\%. Displacements, velocities, momenta, redshift-space multipoles, bispectra and the halo and void abundances are similarly well predicted. For most models we consider, we achieve subpercent error in the power spectrum up to scales $k\lesssim1\,h\,{\rm Mpc}^{-1}$ at all redshifts, with density stochasticity below 0.03\% over the same scales. The method allows constant-$w$ simulations and field-level emulators to be used for CPL cosmologies, and generalises to any cosmology with no additional scale dependence.

papers.title: Finite Temperature Isoscalar Instabilities and Moat Regimes in Relativistic Nuclear Matter
papers.abstract: We study the finite-temperature isoscalar collective response of symmetric nuclear matter in three relativistic mean-field descriptions: the linear Walecka model, its nonlinear extension, and the quark-meson coupling (QMC) model. The Walecka models are formulated in terms of nucle- onic degrees of freedom, whereas QMC incorporates quark degrees of freedom confined inside the nucleon. These models differ in their treatment of scalar interactions at finite density, affecting instability boundaries. Focusing on the coupled scalar-vector channel, we track how the boundaries of homogeneous instabilities evolve with temperature. In all three models, we find a nonmonotonic momentum dependence of the static response, characterized by a minimum at finite momentum, a moat regime that selects a preferred length scale for density fluctuations. Our results show that this moat structure is robust against thermal effects across these relativistic nuclear matter models, providing motivation for future studies of inhomogeneous phases in hot and dense astrophysical matter.

papers.title: Tidal effects of bulk viscosity in neutron stars
papers.abstract: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter provides a temperature-dependent mechanism for tidal dissipation. In this study, we investigate the impact of bulk viscosity on the dissipative tidal response of neutron stars composed of neutrons, protons, and electrons. Employing cold equations of state derived through the momentum-dependent interaction model, we examine the bulk viscosity arising from the direct Urca process, which acts to restore chemical equilibrium. The temperature dependence is incorporated through the weak-interaction rate, allowing us to explore the behavior of bulk viscosity in the neutrino-transparent regime at temperatures up to a few MeV. To account for the spatial distribution of bulk viscosity within neutron stars, we introduce the effective bulk viscosity, a volume-averaged quantity over the region where direct Urca process operates, and establish a connection with the bulk viscosity. Specifically, we investigate its implications for tidal quantities, including the lag time and dissipative deformability, highlighting their dependence on temperature and stellar compactness. We find that the dissipative tidal effects become maximal at a temperature approximately coinciding with the one of maximum bulk viscosity on the onset of direct Urca. Additionally, these effects are more pronounced in intermediate neutron star masses compared to maximum ones. Finally, for both canonical $1.4\;M_\odot$ and maximum-mass neutron star configurations, we derive causality-based upper bounds on these quantities, providing theoretical benchmarks for assessing the potential observability of bulk-viscous effects in gravitational-wave signals from binary neutron star inspirals.

papers.title: Modeling the chemical impacts of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes
papers.abstract: Some protostars undergo episodic accretion, resulting in luminosity outbursts that heat their envelopes. The increase in temperature alters the position of the snowlines, which return to their original locations on different timescales depending on the species. However, the chemical effects of luminosity outbursts in protostellar envelopes, including their long-term consequences, remain poorly explored. We investigate the chemical impact of luminosity outbursts on the envelope of a solar-type protostar, accounting for its dynamics, and identify trends in the molecular response relative to both ongoing and past outburst activity. We combined the dynamic semi-analytic code APE with the three-phase chemical model NAUTILUS to predict the time evolution of 83 molecular abundances between 10 and 10,000 au in the collapsing envelope. The outburst was parameterized by increasing the protostellar luminosity by a factor of 100 for 100 years. The outburst shifts molecular snowlines outward by up to a factor of ten, thus enriching the gas phase through thermal desorption. Most species return to their pre-outburst state within a few thousand years at most for r$\leq$1000 au and remain in that state thereafter. However, eight molecules (HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, C2H5CHO, OCS, SO2, C2S, C3S, and HC3N) show abundance deviations 10$-$50 kyr after the outburst in the warm inner regions (T$\geq$100 K), due to the inward transport of chemically altered material. Eight other species (CH3O, C2O, NH2, HCCO, HCNO, HNO, NO, and NCO) show enhanced gas-phase abundances at intermediate radii ($\sim$300$-$1500 au). Overall, most molecules are impacted by outward snowline shifts. With the exception of HOCH2CHO, CH3COCH2OH, and C2H5CHO, all complex organic molecules (COMs) are expected to exhibit similar abundances in the warm inner regions of protostars (hot corino), regardless of whether they undergo outbursts.

papers.title: Accuracy, Convergence and Consistency of Dark Matter Evolution with the PhotoNs-3 Code
papers.abstract: We systematically investigate the accuracy and convergence of PhotoNs-3, a cosmological N-body code employed for the HyperMillennium simulation. In particular, we examine its convergence with respect to parameters that affect the accuracy of the force calculation and the time evolution, such as the softening length and the adaptive time-stepping scheme, and find that it converges very well. Furthermore, using GADGET as the benchmark, we design four sets of simulations to compare the mutual consistency. We compare the power spectrum of the density field, halo density profiles, and the halo and subhalo mass functions. The difference between PhotoNs-3 and the Gadget codes is at the same level as that between Gadget-3 and Gadget-4. Meanwhile, PhotoNs-3 generally achieves a significant computational speedup. This work establishes that the accuracy and reliability of PhotoNs-3 and its simulations are sufficient for Stage IV galaxy surveys.

papers.title: A hybrid effective field theory description of diffuse baryons
papers.abstract: Galaxy feedback mechanisms that displace baryonic gas on large scales are a dominant uncertainty in many cosmological analyses. Measurements that directly probe the baryonic component, such as Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measure (FRB DM) and the kinetic Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect, can therefore be used to place constraints on feedback and inform other analyses, such as weak lensing. Thus far, analytic methods to model the effects of feedback are either limited to large scales, missing the regime of high signal-to-noise, or have many parameters, weakening constraining power. We propose a Hybrid Effective Field Theory (HEFT) approach, relying on the full gravitational displacement field computed in an $N$-body simulation. We account for feedback via a Lorentzian suppression with a single effective parameter, $c_f^2$. To describe the diffuse baryon field, we extend the arguments by Andrew et al. (arXiv:2604.25828), leveraging most baryons being in a diffuse state to reduce a full bias expansion to just the linear bias, $b_{1,d}^L$. With just these two parameters, we fit the diffuse gas power spectrum in most variants of the FLAMINGO suite of cosmological simulations at percent-level accuracy out to $k=1\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at redshift $z=0.5$ and $k=1.5\,h/\mathrm{Mpc}$ at $z=1$. Further, by fitting the diffuse gas power spectrum including terms argued to be negligible, we show that their contribution is minimal. Applying this prescription for diffuse electron gas enables constraints on both cosmology and astrophysics without the need to marginalize over many unknown parameters.

papers.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
papers.abstract: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.

papers.title: Exploring the phase diagram of dense and hot matter with HBT interferometry
papers.abstract: We investigate the HBT radii of pions produced in Au+Au collisions at selected energies from the STAR-BES program, using an event-by-event hybrid model that combines AMPT initial conditions, 3+1D viscous hydrodynamic evolution with a QCD equation of state at finite baryon chemical potential, and hadronic transport with SMASH. The goal is to explore the source's space-time structure and its possible connection to the structure of the QCD phase diagram. The hybrid chain was first validated by comparing identified-particle spectra and anisotropic flow, yielding a globally consistent description of the experimental data, with more evident discrepancies at the lowest energies.

papers.title: Photomeson-threshold origin of the TeV break in astrophysical neutrinos: Spectrum, flavor, resolved sources, and the ultrahigh-energy landscape
papers.abstract:
IceCube observes a break near 30 TeV in the diffuse astrophysical neutrino spectrum. We interpret it as the photomeson ($p\gamma$) threshold. Accelerated protons interact with the soft x rays of accreting black holes through the $\Delta(1232)$ resonance. One kinematic relation sets the break energy from the target field's lowest photon energy, the seed scale $\varepsilon_0$. The measured break fixes $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.13$ keV and supplies the low-energy suppression no sum of falling power laws can produce. Building on the $\Delta(1232)$ identification of Khatee Zathul, Fang, Halzen, and Hooper and the single-source-class photo-pion fit of Winter, Fiorillo, and Buson, we give closed-form relations that invert the four broken-power-law parameters to the source physics with no remaining freedom, namely, $\gamma_2=s$ and $\gamma_1=s-(\alpha_x-1)$ ($s$, $\alpha_x$ the proton and target photon indices), and $E_{m br}\propto[(1+ ar z)\varepsilon_0]^{-1}$. The break width bounds the total smearing to $\sigma_s\le0.235$ dex (68% CL), no broader than redshift alone must make it, and the seed scale is the same across sources to within a factor $\lesssim$1.5, which mean-spectrum fits do not provide. Below-break neutrinos are predicted to come on average from higher redshifts than those above. The threshold also fixes the flavor and $
u/ ar
u$ composition, including the energy-dependent $ ar
u_e$ fraction and the Glashow-resonance discriminator of Winter et al., matching current flavor data. Inverted source by source, the relation gives each resolved IceCube source its target photon scale, from the keV coronae of NGC 1068 and PKS 1424+240 to the $\sim$20 eV jet of TXS 0506+056. That two-decade spread means they cannot supply the homogeneous break, which requires a separate, fainter population. KM3-230213A points to a warm-dust target, $\varepsilon_0\simeq0.02$ eV, unless cosmogenic.

papers.title: Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity corrections in Dark Dimension scenario
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermodynamics, dynamical stability, and phenomenological implications of Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet (EGB) black holes in Dark Dimension scenarios with one or two micron-sized extra dimensions. For the asymptotically flat, neutral Boulware-Deser solution with positive Gauss-Bonnet coupling $\alpha$, we derive the mass, Hawking temperature, Wald entropy, and heat capacity in arbitrary dimension $D\ge 5$. A positive-heat-capacity branch arises only in $D=5$, where the temperature peaks at $T_{\max}=1/(8\pi\sqrt{\alpha})$ at $r_h=2\sqrt{\alpha}$ and vanishes in the zero-radius limit at finite mass $M_{\rm lim}=3\pi\alpha/(4G_5)$. For $G_5=(8\pi M_*^3)^{-1}$, $\alpha=M_*^{-2}$, and $M_*\sim 10^{10}$ GeV, this yields $M_{\rm lim}\simeq 1.06\times 10^{-12}$ g. While this branch formally overlaps with classical instability zones, the string ultraviolet cutoff safely suppresses the responsible high-harmonic modes. Assuming a UV completion stabilizes these relics, we show they can constitute all of cold dark matter. We map their observational signatures, highlighting a scalar-induced gravitational-wave peak at 33 THz and the suppression of Hawking bursts. In $D=6$, the heat capacity is negative at all radii. Within a bulk blackbody emission model, we derive the leading large-mass lifetime correction and the small-radius scaling $\tau\propto M_0^3$, compared to $\tau_{\rm GR}\propto M_0^{5/3}$. For $M_*\sim 10$ TeV, we identify distinct collider benchmarks: a steeper energy scaling for the production cross section and a suppressed decay multiplicity ($\langle N \rangle \sim 4$). These provide clear experimental signatures distinguishing 6D EGB gravity from classical General Relativity, mapping the transition toward the string scale.

papers.title: The FRB Population Revisited: Rate, Energy, Evolution, and Host-DM Constraints from the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog
papers.abstract: We present a study that simultaneously fits for key fast radio burst (FRB) population properties using the Second CHIME/FRB Catalog while calibrating for instrumental selection effects. Our inferred volumetric rate at $z=0$ is $1.1^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\times 10^{5}\,{\rm Gpc}^{-3}\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$ above an isotropic-equivalent energy of $10^{39}$ erg and below a scattering timescale of 30 ms at 600 MHz. The evolution of the FRB rate relative to the cosmic star formation rate remains statistically unconstrained. Assuming a Schechter function for the energy distribution, isotropic emission, and 1-GHz emission bandwidth, we find a characteristic maximum energy of $2.0^{+2.6}_{-1.0} \times 10^{41}$ erg and a differential power-law index of $-1.41\,^{+0.27}_{-0.21}({\rm stat.})\,\pm\,0.35({\rm sys.})$. The host galaxy contribution to the observed dispersion measure (DM) is modeled as a log-normal distribution; assuming a total Galactic contribution of 80 $\text{pc cm}^{-3}$, we find a median host-galaxy DM contribution of $199^{+34}_{-36}\;\text{pc cm}^{-3}$ in the rest-frame. Finally, we find that the average FRB spectrum, described by a spectral index of $\alpha=-1.0^{+0.5}_{-0.6}$, is inconsistent with being flat at the $\sim2\sigma$ level. We note an excess of high-S/N bursts at low DMs in the observed sample that is not predicted by the best-fit model. Testing alternative models does not alleviate this tension; future population studies may mitigate this limitation by incorporating robust fluence and redshift measurements.

closest.title: Seeing through the fog: astrophysical priors and the evidence for new physics in pulsar timing arrays

papers.title: Plasma-enabled magnet-free LSW search for eV-scale axions with laser-stimulated regeneration
papers.abstract: In conventional light-shining-through-a-wall (LSW) experiments, strong magnetic fields mediate the conversion of photons into axions and their subsequent reconversion into photons. At eV-scale axion masses, however, photon--axion phase mismatch causes these conversions to lose coherence, substantially reducing the experimental sensitivity. We propose a magnet-free LSW scheme that addresses this limitation via plasma-based axion generation and laser-stimulated regeneration. At low laser intensity, a two-color dispersion-matched source generates axions in a narrow mass range set by the plasma dispersion. At relativistic laser intensity, a single-pulse plasma-broadened source generates axions over a broad mass range, as shown by particle-in-cell simulations. The Fourier spectrum of the source term $\mathbf{E}\cdot\mathbf{B}$ broadens around the laser branch, consistent with mixing between the laser and low-frequency plasma waves. For axion detection behind the wall, a counter-propagating laser stimulates axion decay into a detectable signal photon and a second photon emitted into the laser mode, with the laser frequency chosen to satisfy phase matching. For representative parameters, the requirement of at least one regenerated photon yields projected upper limits on the axion-photon coupling on the order $10^{-7}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$ over $m_a=0.1$--$1\,\mathrm{eV}$.

papers.title: Fast Radio Bursts Co-detected by CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 from 400 to 1530 MHz
papers.abstract: We present a sample of $15$ fast radio bursts (FRBs) that were co-detected by the Deep Synoptic Array (DSA-110) and the Canadian Hydrogen Intensity Mapping Experiment (CHIME) between 2022 and 2024, of which $12$ have channelized voltage data from both instruments and 9 have secure redshifts. All but one are as-yet-non-repeating. Most bursts span the entire bandwidth of each instrument (400-800 MHz for CHIME, 1280-1530 MHz for DSA-110), significantly expanding the number of FRBs known to emit across $>1$ GHz of spectral bandwidth and constraining the spectral evolution of energy and propagation effects. On average, the FRBs exhibit higher spectral energies (up to a factor of $\sim10$) in the CHIME band but are lower in peak flux density due to substantial pulse broadening. The sample mean (median) spectral index $-0.4\pm0.4$ ($-0.3\pm0.4$) is shallower than previously reported spectral indices, likely a selection effect. A third of the sample shows evidence for a spectral turnover, comparable to that seen in GHz-peaked pulsar and magnetar spectra. Joint scintillation and pulse broadening constraints indicate that nearly all bursts encounter multiple scattering screens, with pulse broadening originating within their host galaxies. The co-detected bursts are among the most scattered in the CHIME/FRB sample, while being the narrowest in the DSA-110 sample, indicating that CHIME/FRB and DSA-110 select different subsets of the FRB population; the interplay between intrinsic burst width, scattering, and the FRB search time resolution creates a narrow window of sensitivity to co-detected FRBs, providing a blueprint for future ultra-wideband FRB surveys.

papers.title: Closure of averaged Einstein equations by DESI data
papers.abstract: We benchmark the hypothesis that the redshift dependence of postulated dark energy in the standard model, measured by the DESI collaboration, is a natural outcome of dark energy-free models of structure formation in general relativity. We recall fundamental results and the properties of averaged dust cosmologies that suggest to replace the dark energy equation of state through the nonperturbative impact of the inhomogeneous geometry. The relevant mechanism can be phrased in terms of an effective mean field description of inhomogeneities using the fluid analogy of a scalar field (the `morphon'). Without violating energy conditions this effective field exhibits a cross-over to phantom behaviour, compatible with observations. The exact dark energy-free framework needs a single closure condition that we implement in terms of parametrizations of the 3-years data of the DESI team. The resulting redshift dependence of effective cosmological characteristics is then illustrated and subject to physical interpretation. The aim of this paper is to set a benchmark that has to be met by any structure formation model or simulation investigated within general relativity in a flow-orthogonal foliation of spacetime, given the hypothesis.

papers.title: A Transformer-based Method for Neutrino Event Generator Reweighting
papers.abstract: The ability to test the effects of different neutrino event generators on simulation-based analyses is currently bottlenecked by the computational cost of propagating simulated events through expensive detector simulations. One way to circumvent this limitation is to reweight events produced with one generator to replicate the predictions of another. However, existing methods for doing this in neutrino physics tend to be limited to only a few observables at a time. We present a transformer-based architecture that can reweight between neutrino event generators based on nearly the entire particle stack, providing reweighted events that are valid over a greatly expanded phase space. We present results with events generated from multiple GENIE configurations and NuWro as examples, and we introduce an energy distance-based metric for evaluating the results in a multidimensional, unbinned manner. Our results show promising performance for realistic applications and provide a method for comparing the performance of different reweighting techniques.

papers.title: Vector boson scattering in composite Higgs models
papers.abstract: Vector boson scattering is a powerful tool to test the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. We focus on Composite Higgs models with an underlying fermionic description and assume that only one pseudo Nambu-Goldstone boson contributes to electroweak symmetry breaking, which we identify as the Higgs state of the Standard Model. In these scenarios, LHC data imply lower bounds on the predicted resonances below 2 TeV depending on the scenario. Using $WZjj$ production as a benchmark, we demonstrate that the tails of various distributions nevertheless show significant deviations from Standard Model predictions. This holds in particular for the case of longitudinally polarised vector bosons.

papers.title: Probabilistic foreground diagnostics from dispersion measure excess in individual fast radio bursts
papers.abstract: Fast radio bursts (FRBs) provide a unique probe of diffuse baryons through their dispersion measure (DM), but interpreting a large DM for an individual burst is limited by the uncertain contribution from its host galaxy, which is hard to directly observed. We address this gap with a source-level diagnostic framework that treats $\mathrm{DM_{host}}$ as a latent variable drawn from a shared lognormal population, thereby marginalizing over the uncertain host contribution. Applying an expectation--maximization (EM) inference scheme to 92 localized FRBs, we jointly estimate the host-DM population and obtain a model-conditioned host-DM distribution for each burst. We propagate these distributions into an excess cosmological DM for each sightline, quantifying both its uncertainty and the probability that a positive excess remains after accounting for the host contribution. FRBs previously reported to show evidence for foreground or intervening contributions preferentially exhibit high probabilities of retaining such an excess, indicating that this source-level probability can provide a useful statistic for prioritizing foreground follow-up observations. Using this diagnostic, we identify 18 additional localized FRBs as high-priority candidates for follow-up searches for possible intervening galaxies, groups, clusters, or large-scale structure.
